chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever takes an oath and says 'No, by the Lord of the Book' and then breaks it, upon him is one expiation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath sworn by the Quran?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq from Imam Ali, clarifies that swearing by the physical Quran (Mus'haf) carries the same legal weight as swearing by Allah, requiring a single expiation (kaffarah) upon breaking it. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between oaths sworn by the Book itself versus other entities, affirming the sanctity of the Quran as a valid witness in legal oaths. The emphasis on 'one' expiation underscores the principle that the Quran, as the direct word of God, does not incur multiple penalties for a single breach.
